item.title: Rethinking Technology Transfer: Ensuring Resilience, Economic Impact and Social Value
item.content:encoded:
James A. Cunningham, Newcastle University

Jungho Kim, Newcastle University

Chiara Marzocchi, University of Padua

Natalya Radko, Newcastle University

Technology transfer from universities and industry drives economic development, yet rapidly evolving research and technological advancements require continuous development of effective structures and processes. Universities must balance generating economic impact while supporting social value creation—a challenge operating across macro (government policies), meso (TTO structures), and micro (individual researcher) levels.

Current technology transfer systems face disruptions from technological change, geopolitical shifts, AI emergence, and intellectual property challenges. Universities are increasingly expected to contribute to societal grand challenges alongside traditional commercialisation, creating tensions between economic and social value creation for TTOs and academic entrepreneurs.

This special issue seeks research rethinking technology transfer paradigms to examine how systems can build resilience, become inclusive, and deliver blended value. Papers should address operational challenges, emerging TTO configurations, required capabilities for transfer actors, and how new technologies and policies shape the future of university-industry knowledge transfer.

item.title: Intellectual Capital in the Entrepreneurial University: Theory and Practice
item.content:encoded:
Universities are increasingly expected to act as entrepreneurial institutions that create value beyond teaching and research through entrepreneurship education, knowledge exchange, technology transfer, academic spin-offs, and wider ecosystem engagement. However, the mechanisms through which these activities generate economic and societal value remain insufficiently understood, particularly across the full pathway from capability formation to third-mission and regional impact. Existing research often examines entrepreneurship education, academic entrepreneurship, university-industry-society collaboration, and ecosystem development in relative isolation, while practice still relies heavily on narrow indicators such as patents, licences, spin-off counts, or commercialisation income.

Appel publié par Journal of Intellectual Capital. Lire l'appel complet sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Entrepreneurship education and entrepreneurial mindset development as intellectual capital formation
  • Curriculum design, educator roles, and innovative approaches in entrepreneurship education
  • Digital and AI-enabled entrepreneurship education as structural capital
  • Academic entrepreneurship and the micro-foundations of entrepreneurial intellectual capital
  • Technology transfer offices as intellectual capital management mechanisms
  • Intellectual capital, spin-offs, and venture creation in university context
  • University-industry-society collaboration and IC-mediated innovation performance
  • Incubators, accelerators, science parks, and entrepreneurial support infrastructures
  • Entrepreneurial ecosystems around universities and ecosystem-level intellectual capital
  • Third-mission impact measurement, reporting, and evaluation through IC frameworks
  • Practitioner metrics, policy frameworks, and the measurement of knowledge exchange
  • Securing intellectual capital in entrepreneurial universities, including IP governance, data governance, cyber risk, and knowledge leakage
  • International and comparative studies of entrepreneurial university models
  • Multi-level, longitudinal, mixed-method, and engaged research designs in IC and entrepreneurship
